_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.english_concept: fonts to copy / stylish text generator
phrases.content_surface: meta titles, hero copy, FAQ, category pages site-wide
phrases.usage_guidance: Primary head-term phrase; use in titles/H1s for font-conversion pages.
phrases.good_example: Schriftgenerator — Schöne Schrift zum Kopieren, coole Schriftarten & Symbole für Insta, TikTok & Co. (de/index.html title)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a — safe, mainstream, already the site's core term

phrases.content_surface: page titles, WebApplication schema alternateName, hero H1
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the tool/product noun; site already anchors its de.json meta.title on this word.
phrases.good_example: meta.title in locales/de.json: „Schriftgenerator — Schöne Schrift zum Kopieren...“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: library pages, FAQ, symbol pages, forum questions
phrases.usage_guidance: Umbrella term for symbols/glyphs; pair with 'zum Kopieren' for the copy-paste job, or 'im Namen'/'im Nutzernamen' for the naming job.
phrases.good_example: de/gotische-schrift FAQ: „Manche @-Benutzernamen-Felder filtern Sonderzeichen heraus“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a — core vocabulary

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the umbrella term on a dedicated resource page; 'leeres Zeichen' is the more colloquial Discord-specific variant users actually type into forums.
phrases.good_example: de/unsichtbares-zeichen H1: „Unsichtbares Zeichen & Unsichtbarer Text“; FAQ: „Wie mache ich einen unsichtbaren Namen in Free Fire oder Mobile Legends?“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.register: informal, spoken-language phrasing typed into a search box
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in FAQ answers or long-tail H3s targeting the exact colloquial phrasing people type, distinct from the more formal 'unsichtbares Zeichen' umbrella term.
phrases.good_example: gutefrage.net/frage/leeres-zeichen-fuer-discord (thread title: „Leeres Zeichen für Discord?“)
phrases.avoid_when: on a formal/umbrella H1 — use unsichtbares Zeichen there instead

phrases.content_surface: dedicated category page (title, H1, FAQ, WebApplication schema)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the umbrella head-term on the category page; the FAQ itself explains the Gotisch/Fraktur/Textura relationship so users self-serve the nuance.
phrases.good_example: de/gotische-schrift title: „Gotische Schrift Generator — 𝓐𝕔𝔥𝔦𝔴𝔡𝔦 𝕾𝔥𝔡𝔦𝔨𝔵 zum Kopieren“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: on-page FAQ nuance, competitor generator branding
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to add typographic precision/authority in FAQ copy (already done well on de/gotische-schrift), distinguishing it from the broader 'gotische Schrift' umbrella and from Sütterlin (handwriting, not print).
phrases.good_example: de/gotische-schrift FAQ: „Fraktur und die verwandte Textura sind konkrete altdeutsche Ausprägungen davon“
phrases.avoid_when: when the audience means the loose colloquial 'old German look' — use 'gotische Schrift' or 'altdeutsche Schrift' instead

phrases.register: informal/everyday, most common actual search phrasing
phrases.content_surface: WebApplication alternateName, hero copy, forum questions
phrases.usage_guidance: REVISED 2026-07-26 (supersedes the 2026-07-25 guidance below). Promote this to the page's TITLE, H1 and slug, not just alternateName/meta. Prior guidance -- 'keep it prominent in alternateName/meta even though the page's primary H1 uses Gotische Schrift' -- was followed and did not work: 26 days of GSC show the German blackletter cluster earning ~0 clicks while three competitors rank dedicated Altdeutsch/Fraktur pages carrying the term in title+H1+slug (one on an exact-match domain). alternateName is not a ranking surface.
phrases.good_example: gutefrage.net/frage/schriftgenerator-kostenlos-gesucht-fuer-altdeutsche-schriftart („Schriftgenerator kostenlos gesucht für altdeutsche Schriftart“)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.english_concept: Sütterlin script / 'German script' (handwriting, distinct from Fraktur print type)
phrases.usage_guidance: Useful as an FAQ aside on the gotische-schrift page to explain WHY 'Fraktur' and 'Sütterlin' aren't quite the same thing (one is print, one is handwriting) — adds authenticity/authority without needing a separate page, since UTG's Unicode output can only approximate the print (Fraktur) family, not true Sütterlin cursive.
phrases.avoid_when: don't claim UTG's Fraktur-Unicode output IS Sütterlin — it visually is not (Sütterlin is a cursive hand, not a Unicode blackletter block)

phrases.content_surface: FAQ items across many pages, forum threads
phrases.usage_guidance: Standard FAQ pattern already used correctly site-wide: explain cause (no glyph on device), then recommend a safer classic style (Bold/Bubble/Italic).
phrases.good_example: de/index.html FAQ: „Warum sieht meine Schrift bei manchen Leuten wie Kästchen aus?“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.register: neutral, slightly technical (matches actual error-message language)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in FAQ/troubleshooting copy explaining why a styled Unicode name got rejected by a platform's username field (as opposed to the display-name field, which usually accepts it) — pairs naturally with the site's existing @-Benutzername vs. Anzeigename distinction.
phrases.good_example: forum.ubuntuusers.de (directly fetched): „Nach Eingabe von Benutzername und Passwort erscheint die Meldung 'Benutzername enthält ungültige Zeichen'.“ — resolved as „Habe gerade gesehen, dass nur Kleinbuchstaben und Ziffern verwendet werden dürfen.“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Strong head-term candidate for a game-name generator page/section; independently confirmed across at least 4 separate platform-specific forum threads, so it generalizes rather than being one game's quirk.
phrases.good_example: gutefrage.net/frage/nicknames-mit-sonderzeichen-erstellen; gutefrage.net/frage/ps4-fortnite-namen-aendern-mit-sonderzeichen; gutefrage.net/frage/call-of-duty-namen-aendern-mit-sonderzeichen; gutefrage.net/frage/online-id-sonderzeichen
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'cool' (borrowed, fully naturalized in German youth/gaming speech) rather than a stiffer native synonym like 'toll' or 'super' for this specific audience/context.
phrases.good_example: gutefrage.net/frage/coole-nicknames-fuer-gamesspiele; gutefrage.net/frage/wie-kommt-man-auf-coole-gaming-namen; gutefrage.net/frage/gute-nicknames-fuer-spiele
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Standard, safe, dictionary-correct word for 'unique' — pairs well as the positive counterpart to the '08/15' idiom (DE-016) for copy that wants both a plain-language and a culturally-flavored option.
phrases.good_example: gutefrage.net/frage/was-bedeutet-einzigartig-fuer-euch; gutefrage.net/frage/wie-wuerdet-ihr-einen-schmuckladen-nennen-der-name-soll-einzigartig-sein-mit-wiedererkennungswert
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Already used correctly and naturally on-site; keep pairing it with 'Profilnamen' as the site does, since a clan tag alone is rarely the whole ask.
phrases.good_example: de/gotische-schrift/index.html: „Gestalte einen markanten Profilnamen, einen Clan-Tag für Discord und Games“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.register: neutral, matches Discord's own DE localization
phrases.content_surface: FAQ, on-page copy across multiple pages
phrases.usage_guidance: Always quote as Discord's own field label (in guillemets/quotes as the site already does: »Über mich«) rather than inventing a paraphrase, so users can map it 1:1 to the Discord UI.
phrases.good_example: de/usecase/bio-schriftart FAQ: „Discords »Über mich« unterstützt bis zu 190 Zeichen“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Central to the site's most important accuracy claim (Anzeigename accepts Unicode, @Benutzername does not) — keep this distinction sharp and consistent, it's already well-executed.
phrases.good_example: de/guide/discord-textformatierung-erklaert comparison table: „Meinen Anzeigenamen oder Nickname gestalten → Unicode-Schrift (einfügen)“ vs. „Das Aussehen meines eindeutigen @Benutzernamens ändern → Nicht möglich“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Always pair with the explicit charset rule (a–z, 0–9, underscore, dot) so the FAQ resolves the confusion in one read, as the site already does consistently.
phrases.good_example: de/schriftarten-fuer-tiktok FAQ: „Der Benutzername (der eindeutige @-Handle) akzeptiert nur Kleinbuchstaben von a bis z, Zahlen, Unterstrich und Punkt“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Page already generalizes well beyond social platforms into academic use ('Hausarbeit oder Klausur') — a genuinely DE-market-relevant extension (character-count-based academic submission limits) not seen in the EN equivalent's likely framing.
phrases.good_example: de/woerter-zeichen-zaehlen FAQ: „Wie viele Zeichen darf eine Hausarbeit oder Klausur haben?“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.usage_guidance: Very strong, repeated head-term pattern specific to WhatsApp; worth a dedicated FAQ entry or H2 clarifying WhatsApp has no native font picker and that copy-paste Unicode is the actual mechanism, mirroring how the Discord pages already de-confuse Nitro vs. Unicode.
phrases.good_example: gutefrage.net/frage/schrift-aendern-bei-whatsapp-; gutefrage.net/frage/wie-kann-man-bei-whatsapp-seine-schrift-aendern; gutefrage.net/frage/schrift-aendern-bei-whatsapp-status
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: forum meta-discussions about the word itself, and direct application ('Ist mein Name cringe?')
phrases.usage_guidance: German youth culture has fully adopted 'cringe' as a loanword precisely because, per gutefrage discussion, German has no single native word that captures the same meaning — 'peinlich' is the closest native equivalent but isn't a perfect synonym. Useful for FAQ copy warning against over-decorating a name/bio ('bevor es cringe wirkt').
phrases.good_example: gutefrage.net/frage/ist-mein-name-cringe („Ist mein Name cringe?“); gutefrage.net/frage/was-heisst-cringe-3 discussion noting 'peinlich' as the nearest native match
phrases.avoid_when: in more formal/authority-building guide content aimed at an older or professional audience — use 'übertrieben' or 'zu viel des Guten' there instead

phrases.content_surface: dedicated category page, tattoo/bio usecase pages
phrases.usage_guidance: Correctly kept distinct from 'kursive Schrift' (italic — a different, narrower style) on this site; this distinction matters because German 'kursiv' means italic specifically, not cursive-script, unlike casual English usage where 'cursive' and 'italic' sometimes blur.
phrases.good_example: de/usecase/tattoo-schrift FAQ: „Die Schreibschrift ist der Klassiker fürs Namens-Tattoo“
phrases.avoid_when: don't use interchangeably with 'kursive Schrift' — they name different styles on this site and in general German usage

phrases.english_concept: aesthetic style (borrowed English adjective as style name)
phrases.usage_guidance: Site smartly keeps the untranslated English loanword 'Aesthetic' in the page title/H1 (matching how the term is actually used/searched) while using the native adjective 'ästhetische' in descriptive body prose — a good dual-register pattern worth replicating for other borrowed style-names.
phrases.good_example: de/aesthetic-schrift title: „Aesthetic Schrift Generator — ａｅｓｔｈｅｔｉｃ Ｓｃｈｒｉｆｔ zum Kopieren“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.content_surface: dedicated usecase page with rich FAQ
phrases.usage_guidance: The page's FAQ is unusually well-crafted for a generator site: it explicitly warns the Unicode output is 'eine Arbeitsgrundlage, keine stichfertige Vorlage' (a starting point, not a ready-to-ink template) and flags the umlaut/ß rendering gap for tattoo artists — a genuinely German-market-specific caveat (ä/ö/ü/ß have no Fraktur/script Unicode forms) worth preserving as house style for any future tattoo-adjacent content.
phrases.good_example: de/usecase/tattoo-schrift FAQ: „Achtung bei Umlauten: ä, ö, ü und ß bleiben in den Unicode-Schriften meist normale Buchstaben, aber dein Tätowierer zeichnet sie im finalen Lettering problemlos mit.“
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.english_concept: romantic font for a love letter
phrases.usage_guidance: A genuinely distinct occasion-based angle from tattoo/gaming/bio use cases already covered; Schreibschrift is the consistent answer across both this thread and the existing wedding-forum evidence (EV-186 in de-existing.json), reinforcing Schreibschrift as THE romantic-occasion recommendation.
phrases.good_example: gutefrage.net/frage/mit-welcher-schriftart-ist-es-am-besten-einen-liebesbrief-zu-schreiben-schreibschriftblockschrift- (asks specifically Schreibschrift vs. Blockschrift for a love letter)
phrases.avoid_when: n/a

phrases.english_concept: bubble letters (the rounded, inflated letter style)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use the English term as the head term on a de printables page, with a German gloss beside it ('Bubble Letters (fluffige Buchstaben zum Ausmalen)'). Half-German hybrids like 'Bubble-Schrift' are attested and safe; a fully German compound is not.
phrases.good_example: Bubble Letters zum Ausdrucken: fluffige Buchstaben zum Ausmalen.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in copy for older/formal audiences where an unglossed anglicism reads as marketing filler; always pair with the German description on first use.

phrases.native_phrase: Ausgangsschrift — Schulausgangsschrift (SAS) / Vereinfachte Ausgangsschrift (VA) / Lateinische Ausgangsschrift (LA) / Grundschrift
phrases.english_concept: the specific named cursive script a German school teaches
phrases.register: neutral, pedagogical — but the *question form* is fully parent-facing
phrases.content_surface: faq, body, guide-style section, tool selector labels
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the strongest German finding for the cursive-printables cluster. A de handwriting-sheet page that offers only one generic 'Schreibschrift' is answering a question German parents do not have; the locally native framing is to name the script (SAS / VA / LA / Grundschrift) and say that it varies by Bundesland. Use 'Schreibschrift' as the H1 head term (it is what people search first) and the named scripts in FAQ/selector copy.
phrases.good_example: Welche Schreibschrift lernt mein Kind — SAS, VA oder Grundschrift? Die Ausgangsschrift ist von Bundesland zu Bundesland unterschiedlich.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not assert which script a given school uses — it varies by Bundesland and by school, and getting it wrong is worse than staying general. Do not use these names for decorative/Unicode cursive styling: they are handwriting models, not fonts to copy-paste, and DE-026 ('Schreibschrift') already covers the decorative sense. Not applicable outside DE — Austria and Switzerland have their own school scripts, which this pass did not research.

phrases.english_concept: a lettering tattoo (the tattooed word/name/quote itself, as opposed to the font)
phrases.register: neutral — genuinely shared between studio and customer
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the *thing being made* ('dein Schriftzug am Handgelenk'), and keep 'Tattoo Schrift' (DE-028) for the *style being chosen*. Keeping the two apart is what makes the German page read as written by someone who has been in a studio.
phrases.good_example: Ein Zitat, ein Name, ein einzelnes Wort — so wirkt dein Schriftzug am Handgelenk.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'Schriftzug' where 'Schriftart'/'Schrift' is meant (a font in a dropdown is not a Schriftzug). Outside tattoo context 'Schriftzug' most often means a brand wordmark/logo lettering, so do not carry it onto the general font-generator pages.

phrases.register: studio-professional and consumer; strongly associated with small/delicate tattoos
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the German name for the thin/delicate style row on the tattoo page, capitalised and hyphen-compounded German-style ('Fineline-Schriftzug'). It pairs naturally with the wrist/collarbone placement copy.
phrases.good_example: Für ein zartes Fineline-Tattoo am Handgelenk passt eine dünne Schreibschrift besser als eine Fraktur.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use it to mean 'small'. Do not use it on non-tattoo pages. Do not write it as two words ('fine line') in German copy — German sources compound it.

phrases.english_concept: kaomoji / text-built emoticon as a named thing
phrases.content_surface: h1 (as 'Kaomoji'), first-paragraph gloss, faq, section headings
phrases.usage_guidance: Head the page with 'Kaomoji' (the query people who know the thing type) and gloss it in sentence one as 'japanische Text-Emoticons'. Use 'westliche Smileys' when contrasting with :-). Do NOT invent 'Textgesichter' as a German head term — I found no organic German usage of it.
phrases.good_example: Kaomoji sind japanische Text-Emoticons: Im Gegensatz zu westlichen Smileys wie :-) werden sie aufrecht dargestellt.
phrases.avoid_when: Don't use 'Text-Emoticons' where 'Emojis' is meant (graphical). Don't use it as the label for ASCII pictures — Germans have separate, more natural words for those (see the Zeichenbilder record).

phrases.english_concept: the shrug ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ as its own searched item
phrases.register: casual internet German; mainstream enough for journalism
phrases.usage_guidance: For a German shrug page: 'Schulterzucken-Emoji ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ kopieren' in the title (matches the descriptive query) and 'Shruggie' as the named-term variant inside the body/H2. Note in copy that it is NOT an emoji but a Unicode character string — German pages consistently make that correction and it is a real FAQ.
phrases.good_example: Das Shruggie ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ ist kein Emoji, sondern eine Kombination aus Unicode-Zeichen — das Gesicht in der Mitte ist das japanische Katakana ツ.
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid 'Shruggie' alone in formal/technical or accessibility copy — use 'Schulterzucken-Zeichenfolge' or spell out the construction. Avoid 'Achselzucken' in youth-facing copy; it reads stiff/anatomical.

phrases.english_concept: ASCII art — a picture built out of characters
phrases.usage_guidance: Title on 'ASCII-Art' (the query with volume and the term the SERP is built around) but make the visible H1/subhead carry 'Bilder aus Zeichen zum Kopieren' so the plain-language searcher recognises the page. 'Zeichenbilder' and 'Buchstabenbilder' work as category labels.
phrases.good_example: ASCII-Art zum Kopieren: schöne Bilder aus Zeichen und Buchstaben für WhatsApp, Discord und Foren.
phrases.avoid_when: Don't use it for single face emoticons (that's Text-Emoticons/Kaomoji). Don't use 'Zeichenbilder' in technical copy about encodings — 'Zeichen' there means codepoint and the pun is confusing.

phrases.english_concept: hand-lettering as a practice distinct from calligraphy
phrases.usage_guidance: Use only in an FAQ that clarifies what the tool is not ('kein Handlettering und keine Kalligrafie — fertige Unicode-Zeichen zum Kopieren'). The spelling matters: 'Handlettering' as one capitalised word. Do not target it — the SERP is courses and supplies.
phrases.good_example: Beim Handlettering zeichnet man die Buchstaben; dafür braucht man nicht unbedingt eine Feder.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Never as a claim about the site's output.

phrases.english_concept: professional-risk objection: styled Unicode looks unprofessional/dodgy
phrases.content_surface: faq, body copy, honest 'when not to use this' sections
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to name the objection the reader already has, in a FAQ answer that then gives balanced guidance. It supports an honesty/limitations section — never a title, never a selling point.
phrases.good_example: Im professionellen Umfeld wirken solche optischen Spielereien schnell unseriös — deshalb: maximal ein bis zwei Kernaussagen hervorheben.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in gaming, aesthetic, or teen-facing copy — DE-024 (cringe/peinlich) is the register-appropriate criticism there. Do not use it to describe the tool itself; it describes the *overuse* of the output.

phrases.english_concept: what the Unicode bold/italic characters actually are, in accessibility discourse
phrases.content_surface: faq, body copy, technical explainer sections
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in the explanation of *why* screen readers stumble. It earns credibility precisely because it is more specific than 'Sonderzeichen'. Do not lead a page with it — it is an explanatory term, not a search term.
phrases.good_example: Denn zur Anwendung gelangen mathematische Sonderzeichen — und deutsche Umlaute sind dort nicht vorhanden.
phrases.avoid_when: Not a search-facing head term; a German user looking for the tool types 'Schriftarten zum Kopieren' (DE-001), never this. Do not use in casual/gaming copy.

phrases.usage_guidance: Write 'ATS' for findability and 'Bewerbermanagement-Software' on first gloss. Use 'Datensalat' only in an explanatory sentence about what goes wrong; it is colloquial and would be out of place in a heading.
phrases.good_example: Sterne-Bewertungen und kreisförmige Diagramme sehen modern aus, sind für ATS aber unsichtbar.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use in social/gaming copy. Do not claim a specific rejection rate or percentage — the figures floating around German ATS blogs are unverified.

phrases.english_concept: writing bio/profile text stacked one item per line (the decorative-vertical job as it actually exists in this market)
phrases.register: neutral-casual; the Q&A voice of gutefrage/Quora askers and of consumer how-to blogs
phrases.content_surface: h2, faq heading, tool copy, body
phrases.usage_guidance: Use «untereinander schreiben» as the German-facing name of the feature/section and «Zeilenumbruch» as the term inside the tool UI and the technical explanation — that split matches how the market splits: users search the layout, tools label the mechanism. A German page that leads with 'vertikaler Text' will not meet this query at all.
phrases.good_example: So kannst du deine Instagram-Bio untereinander schreiben — mit einem echten Zeilenumbruch statt Leerzeichen.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use it for CJK-style vertical writing or for a one-letter-per-line effect — 'untereinander' describes lines/items, and using it for stacked single letters will read as a different, non-existent feature. Do not use 'Absatz' when the tool actually inserts a single line break rather than a paragraph break; German users notice the difference in the resulting spacing.

phrases.native_phrase: Zeichen mit/ohne Leerzeichen; Anschläge; Normzeile; Normseite
phrases.english_concept: characters incl./excl. spaces + German billing units
phrases.usage_guidance: 'mit oder ohne Leerzeichen' is the recurring GuteFrage question verbatim; a ÷55 / ÷1800 readout serves the billing job. Also note Word excludes Fußnoten by default — documented grade damage.
phrases.avoid_when: gaming copy

phrases.english_concept: colloquial short form of "Schriftarten für Instagram" -- a small, real naming sub-niche flagged in 2026-07 but never threaded into production copy
phrases.usage_guidance: H2/body-copy phrasing or FAQ aside on de/schriftarten-fuer-instagram and de/usecase/bio-schriftart -- not a title/H1 replacement for the existing head terms.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not stack alongside the page's existing primary head term ("Schriftarten für Instagram") in the same title/H1 -- same near-synonym-stacking caution already recorded for DE-033/034.

phrases.usage_guidance: German attaches "zum Kopieren" rather than a verb phrase: sonderzeichen zum kopieren 1,900/mo, herzen zum kopieren 1,000/mo.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use as the primary H1 term — the head noun (Sonderzeichen, Herzen) carries the ranking; this qualifies it.
